messages.subject: Nblast Parameter Advice
parts:
I am attempting to use Nblast as a metric to compare the accuracy of automatic neuron reconstruction algorithms for dendritic morphology of mice neurons. So I have an SWC for the neuron manually marked up, as well as an SWC of the neuron automatically reconstructed, and would like to see how well the automatic algorithm fared. 

I am looking for advice on what parameters of Nblast would be most appropriate for this specific use case. For example, 'smat', 'sd', 'version', 'UseAlpha', etc...

Thanks for your help,
Corey Elowsky

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Nblast Parameter Advice
parts:
Dear Corey,

Thanks for your message and interest in NBLAST. It is not clear to me that NBLAST will be the best metric for your purposes. NBLAST was designed for rapid comparison of different neurons and it considers only neurite position and local geometry but not topology. 

In the case of looking for reconstruction errors, I assume you will have a clear ground truth with topology information and you may wish to consider this as part of your score. That said I am not aware of any particularly sensitive approaches in this area. The DIADEM challenge with which I was involved a few years ago used a rather simple metric.

In any case to try NBLAST, you could take a look at what the recent Gouwens et al preprint from the Allen used. IIRC they used NBLAST v1 with an sd=10µm. I assume they did not use the alpha weighting. If you want to try NBLAST v2 then I would divide the neurons by 3 before NBLASTing to roughly account for the difference in spatial scale. 

All the best,

Greg.
